fixed.explanation: IndexCol.validate_metadata passed dtype_equal=True to array_equivalent. That told it the dtypes match, but int and float categories have different dtypes. The comparison then went to a low-level buffer path and failed with a buffer dtype mismatch. Removing the flag makes array_equivalent compare the dtypes, return False, and so raise the intended different-categories ValueError.

query.intent: PyTables HDFStore categorical append path: when appending to an existing table, the new categories are compared with the stored categories (CategoricalCol / validate_col / validate_metadata / _create_axes). The check must raise the different-categories ValueError before the values are cast or written, instead of a buffer dtype mismatch error.
query.symptom: Appending a categorical with float categories to an HDF5 table with integer categories raises a low-level buffer dtype error instead of the ValueError about differing categories.

history.analysis: Only HDFStore.append/put and Table._create_axes were shown. _create_axes builds the new categorical column and ends with new_table.validate(self). The different-categories check most likely lives in the validation routines (Table.validate, DataCol.validate_metadata/validate_attr), and it probably runs too late or compares only same-dtype categories.

query.intent: Validation code that compares metadata (categories) of an appended column against the existing table's column and raises ValueError about differing categories.
query.symptom: Appending float categories to an HDF5 table with integer categories raises a low-level buffer dtype error instead of the different-categories ValueError.

history.analysis: IndexCol.validate_metadata raises the different-categories ValueError. It calls array_equivalent with dtype_equal=True. That promises the dtypes match, so int and float categories go to a low-level buffer comparison and fail with a buffer dtype mismatch. The fix is to drop dtype_equal=True, or to check the dtypes first.
